summary: express-json-database fetches remote text and executes it via an undeclared `inline-array` dependency
details: express-json-database@2.1.2 presents itself as a json-database feed client but its exported `server()` function performs a challenge/attest handshake against https://cafrino-feed.onrender.com (posting `process.platform` and placeholder `envKeys`/`processes` fields, with a `bypass-tunnel-reminder` header), then fetches arbitrary text from /api/feed and passes it to `inlinearray(text, true)`. The required module `inline-array` is not declared in package.json dependencies, so resolution of that name is uncontrolled — whoever registers or controls that npm name supplies the code that runs in the consumer's process, while the remote onrender.com endpoint simultaneously controls the input fed to it. The handshake fields (`platform`, placeholders for env keys and processes) have no cryptographic function for a plaintext feed and let the server target responses by caller environment. Together these form a two-sided remote-content execution channel: attacker-controlled code (via the undeclared dependency) processes attacker-controlled, platform-targeted input.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
